axioms: Every duplicated procedure definition is a latent bug: copies drift and users cannot tell which is canonical
Sprawl is measurable by counting how many places encode the same procedure
The smallest consolidation that removes divergence beats any grand unification
Some duplication is load-bearing (different host, different lifecycle) and must be distinguished from accidental copies
A duplicate without a declared canonical home will be improved in one copy and stale in the rest
Template-stamped artifacts are safe only while bodies stay identical; the drift clock is always ticking
failure_mode: Did not diff all ~58 PHILOSOPHY.md/AGENTS.md pairs section-by-section; drift counts came from hash bucketing of the doctrine tail only
Did not compare intercore's Go ic lock internals against interlock's MCP server beyond entry points
~45 interverse plugins outside the deep-dive list got README skims only
Systematically assumes consolidation is safe — may misclassify host/lifecycle-specific divergence as accidental duplication
